spec.name: complete-persona-launch
spec.intent:
Realize the handed persona launch shard, including its enforcement scope and persona closure, as one complete, composition-owned executable launch on Claude Code and omp. The separately handed enforcement scope primitive is already a factor of this shard; its ownership/activation changes are realized here, not duplicated in a second unit. The plan realizes both handed anchors. One terminal wave with one integration owner is intentional: projection, the adapter port, both renderers, worker admission, launch wiring, and their consumers change together. A file-based or harness-based split would overlap the same projector and tests; an ownership-then-launch chain would leave a false intermediate claim of completion. This is a single end-to-end cutover on existing seams, not a new runtime capability or a redesign of the guard prompts. If execution establishes that it exceeds the implementer's dispatch capacity, stop for planner re-cutting against the existing factors; do not hand back a partial unit as complete.

CENSUS, taken once from source commit a327bd6e96f3c92d1dba0242bf886e6abc094cda on 2026-10-02: the source worktree had no tracked implementation changes. Design amendments 01M3ZAHN9C1K8SMCQCA540M8H1 (enforcement scope) and 01M3ZAHNR4MCMTZD4AKYPEA326 (persona launch) were uncommitted; persona is 01M3W846Q2NS8ENRDTY9929N0F. These record versions, not the view header's commit, are the design referent. RecordStore.read unions this checkout and the plan lines; Reading.computed reports the first plan-line worktree's HEAD, which explained a4b440c5 in the interfaces while this source checkout was at the commit above. Binding moves plan/unit and relevant notebook records but not design records, so the planner supplies the pinned design records on the new line before handing out this unit. Do not rederive this census absent intervening changes to its paths.

The supported harness denominator at that commit is the registry's claude and omp. Current purviewGuardrail DOES declare binds:{dimension:'role'}; stance guards also bind composition. The GlobalSessionOrigin claim that purview has no binds is false against this source. project/index.ts discovers hook modules by directory rather than only canon/hook-cells.ts. It carries binds into local sources and stanceManifests, then drops them at the hooks/scopeActivatedSurface registration call. ompScopeActivatedExtensions emits the same guard-bearing registrations at _session and each agent. TURN_BRIDGE derives scope from the module location; the global scope has no manifest. Thus duplicate registration is observed, but duplicate successful judgments are NOT established by those registrations alone. The host manifest and deployed global module were read on 2026-10-02: enforcing:_session records agent/extensions/cratylus-session.ts, and it contains purview and stance registrations. This is active deployment output, not an orphan. Do not delete host files during implementation.

The use census, not just definition sites, is the declared output envelope below. The ownership path runs through core/enrollment.ts (composes, stanceManifests, personaRootOf), core/harness-adapter.ts, project/index.ts, both adapter renderers and barrels, Claude hook serialization, deploy/hooks.ts and manifest/deploy pruning, install/uninstall, persona command placement, worker templates and committed targets. omp registration and filenames are consumed by forge adapter/deploy tests and canon harness-parity/purview tests; skill-cap and launch APIs are consumed by both adapters, projector cap tests and canon skill-hook-cap; worker ingress is exercised by canon purview/stance tests and the hermetic shell suite. Current README claims that Claude guards live in settings and presence alone enrolls are affected. Historical changelog entries, past design/plan/notebook records, rubric calibration fixtures, and the locked ground documents are evidence, not rewrite targets. Existing worker deadline/recovery/contest/stop-loop behavior remains unchanged.

IMPLEMENTATION: resolve every guard's composing agents once using the existing composes and realized-event seam; retain ownership through registration instead of stripping binds. Partition guards from non-enforcing session plumbing before adapter emission. Each agent-owned surface contains only that agent's applicable guard registrations. Deduplicate the union of enforcing-fragment and HookCell routes by guard identity and applicable native trigger/selector so one semantic act cannot invoke one guard through two registrations. Shared worker bytes and a shared launcher are allowed; shared registration authority is not. A bare session and an agent with no applicable guard get no guard handlers. Keep unrelated host hooks/extensions, drift notice, event tap, badge, role routing and dispatch isolation intact. A genuinely unscopable harness keeps the rule as a steer and reports the loss; do not manufacture an always-loaded guard that usually exits.

On omp, the user's native extension directory remains discoverable when a persona overlay is added. Therefore stop placing composition-bound guard handlers in the native session-root module. Let only the selected persona's explicit launch surface activate its guards, using owner-qualified guard module names derived from the CLI bin and persona, with the scope directory and manifest as the authority rather than parsing a display filename. Give session plumbing a truthful, separate surface; do not copy it into every persona merely to mimic profile-era placement. Exercise native discovery plus the overlay together, not only a direct call to one generated module. Retain ctx.agent.kind main-only enforcement and the existing diagnostic for an unknown session kind. Inherited subagent environment is not enrollment. Do not globally disable discovery or suppress unrelated extensions to make the counts come out.

On Claude Code, carry the applicable guards in the selected agent's own native hook body/launch surface rather than user-wide guard registrations that infer authority from agent_type and a discovered namesake manifest. Reuse the native front-matter hook machinery and canonical event mappings; supply the selected installation's explicit scope to the shared worker through the owned command. Preserve the single hooks block, matching selectors, hook order and native subagent exclusion. The worker's scope must come from the selected executable body, not whichever installation contains a same-named persona. Remove the implicit agent_type-to-local-manifest enrollment fallback and validate the guard's own gate/moment in the selected manifest, rather than treating any manifest as permission to run all guards. Derive contract paths from that same owner. Carry the explicit scope consistently through omp's envelope and Claude's owned command; do not introduce a compatibility alias for ambient enrollment.

Complete launch includes identity, the transitive composed skill closure whole before the first turn, and those same applicable guards. Keep one authored agent definition and shared implementation, not per-persona copied logic. Preserve install consent, name-conflict handling, relocation/home behavior, selected model route, runtime skill routes and uninstall attribution. Close any launch path that currently replaces a required skill with a truncation preview or deferred required-reading notice: Claude's existing per-hook cap path and omp's missing/filtered-skill fallback are not evidence of complete delivery. Prefer a native full prompt/file carrier or correctly bounded complete native preload over an invented protocol; help read during this census explicitly documents omp --append-system-prompt accepting file contents and Claude's --bare help names --append-system-prompt[-file]. Resolve exact carrier behavior using the installed harness before claiming it. Do not rewrite guard rubrics, retry policy, role/persona definitions, or unrelated prompt text. A supported named launch must not silently claim completeness with a missing required body.

Clean cutover: reuse manifest-attributed pruning to retire replaced modules and global guard registrations on project/reinstall; do not add a legacy mode or scan-delete foreign files. Update affected callers, barrels, fixture expectations, emitted worker targets, ownership documentation and the package changeset in this same unit. The output list is a contention envelope, not a mandate to touch every file. If another actual consumer or new production file is required, ask the planner to revise the envelope before editing it. Acceptance is confined to this ownership and launch delta; preserve existing guard behavioral regressions, but do not run live rubric calibration. The unit's implementer builds and adds tests; the main integrator runs the listed checks once after the complete unit lands, with no mid-flight build/test/formatter storm.

EXECUTION-ROUTE RECTIFICATION, 2026-10-02, after BuildCompletePersonaLaunch returned without implementation: absent native-loader tests are work this unit owes, not a missing upstream deliverable. The planner observed /home/lex/.local/bin/claude reporting 2.1.285 and /home/lex/.local/bin/omp reporting 18.4.12 from the bound line; both help surfaces are available. No native activation result is claimed by this observation. The pre-existing incomplete skill path and global registration path are the specified defects, not blockers or compatibility constraints. The unit remains active on the same design pin and owns the full cutover.

Author the reusable native exercise in the already-declared test/deploy/complete-persona-launch.test.ts; test/deploy/native-harness.ts is additionally permitted for its shared process/server support. Use absolute paths to the real installed harness executables (allow a test configuration override), temporary HOME and cwd, temporary CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR for Claude, and a temporary default-profile PI_CODING_AGENT_DIR for omp. Remove inherited profile/provider/credential/nested-session environment that would leak the operator's installation or reroute fixture traffic. Deploy through the real projector/placer to these roots. Preserve native discovery and selected-agent hooks: --bare, --safe-mode, --no-extensions, replacement loader factories, or replacing the real harness binary are not valid evidence for the ownership criteria. A neutral sentinel hook/extension in the temporary user root must remain observable beside the selected persona.

The native rig can remain offline and deterministic. Run a loopback HTTP fixture with the Anthropic Messages streaming protocol, capturing the complete incoming system/messages/tool schemas and returning controlled assistant text, harmless tool calls confined to the temporary workspace, native subagent dispatch, and PASS judge answers. This substitutes model nondeterminism only: production launchers, native loaders, event dispatch, scope selection, generated registrations, shared guard workers and judgment transport still execute. A test wrapper that logs then execs the unchanged deployed worker may count invocation; it may not replace admission logic. Identify main, child and judge requests separately and compare first-request identity/skill bytes plus each guard's invocation counts. Start a fresh child harness process per scenario, bound its lifetime, retain useful failure output and clean all child processes/temporary roots in finally. Do not use or print production credentials or call a billed provider for this mechanical proof.

Configuration sources read for this route are omp://extension-loading.md, omp://models.md and omp://system-prompt-customization.md, and https://code.claude.com/docs/en/llm-gateway-connect.md plus https://code.claude.com/docs/en/llm-gateway-protocol.md. omp's native roots are the active agent directory extensions and cwd/.omp/extensions; --config supplies configured paths after those roots, with absolute-path deduplication, not filename deduplication. Its temporary agent-dir models.yml supports a custom provider with baseUrl at loopback, api: anthropic-messages, explicit apiKey/auth: apiKey, and a declared model; route the main model and modelRoles.advisor to that fixture so the in-process judge uses it too. Claude supports ANTHROPIC_BASE_URL with a fixture ANTHROPIC_AUTH_TOKEN; serve /v1/messages including query strings and full SSE completion, optionally count_tokens, and capture requests before any response. Keep all fixture configuration local to the child process and temporary root. These documented routes establish an actionable construction path, not a claimed passing run; handle the installed versions' actual request shapes rather than assuming the newest online docs are identical.

The implementer implements the production change and this real-loader rig; the main/integrator executes it after the coherent change is handed back, under the existing no-mid-flight-verification rule. A return may truthfully say checks were not run by the implementer, but may not call an absent test file or ungenerated evidence an unavailable prerequisite. If a native experiment subsequently establishes a real obstacle, report the exact binary/version, sanitized command and environment, emitted failure, scenario denominator, and which documented alternative was tried; finish reachable production/tests and route that precise finding to the planner. None of this changes the required native-loader/first-turn evidence or authorizes marking the unit complete without it.
accept: Projection matrix enumerates and prints the supported-harness denominator from HARNESS_NAMES, the agent denominator and each guard/moment denominator. For each supported harness, project two differently composed agents plus an unguarded agent and session plumbing; assert exact applicable guard registrations per owner, zero guard registrations in native/global session surfaces, no inherited registration in the unguarded agent, and no duplicate guard/act path across HookCell and enforcing-fragment inputs. Include a deliberately duplicated/widened fixture that this assertion rejects; the current N+1 global guard projection must fail it.

Deployed activation tests load native user surfaces together with the selected persona surface, with another installed persona and another installation containing the same persona name also discoverable. Count actual worker/judge invocations, not file presence: exactly one per applicable guard/trigger of the selected main composition; zero for bare, unbound, foreign-owner and dispatched-subagent cases. Exercise omp native discovery plus --config and Claude selected --agent hooks plus user settings, preserving an unrelated host hook/extension sentinel. Print all cases attempted and completed; unavailable native-loader evidence is a missing criterion, never a pass from a single-module mock.

Worker regressions demonstrate that a selected explicit scope with the guard and moment reaches its own contract and judge; a mere agent_type name plus a neighboring installed manifest does not enroll; a manifest containing only another guard does not enroll this guard; a subagent never judges even with inherited owner context. Use two distinguishable contracts and assert the selected contract bytes reach the judge. Existing fail-open notices, recovery, timeout budget, evidence checks, retry/contest handling and bounded stop behavior remain passing without rubric changes.

Named-launch integration exercises both command symlink and generic launcher forms on claude and omp from a non-install cwd and a relocated/custom home. Before the first model turn, capture the actual selected prompt/preload input and compare identity plus every transitive composed skill body and route, in full, exactly once; include a skill beyond the old Claude hook cap, multibyte content and a diamond closure. Assert the same launch selects only its owned guards. Missing required bodies or an incompatible override must be explicitly diagnosed and cannot be reported as a complete successful launch. Validate the real harness carrier rather than only matching generated shell strings.

Fresh install, reinstall and uninstall tests prove consent/default-no/dry-run placement behavior and non-overwrite of occupied persona names; the deploy record attributes every new owned artifact. Reinstall removes the recorded obsolete global guard registrations/modules and keeps unrelated host files, hooks, extensions and foreign/unrecorded same-named files. Uninstall removes only recorded owned commands/artifacts and leaves unrelated host state unchanged. Repeated project/deploy is idempotent.

All renamed or retired registration/launch exports and callers in the use census are updated; no stale alternate guard enrollment route or duplicate launch/preload path remains. The committed guard shell targets equal the resolved cell outputs. Ownership and complete-launch docs describe the implemented surfaces; a changeset records the affected packages. Historical records/changelogs and judge rubric bodies are unchanged.

After the completed change lands, the main integrator runs pnpm build, pnpm typecheck, pnpm typecheck:test, pnpm lint, pnpm canon:project:targets, pnpm project, pnpm test and pnpm stance-guard:test once in dependency order, formatting only changed paths before committing if needed. Review generation output against the declared footprint; tests print nonzero reach denominators and fail rather than skip a missing render or supported harness. No verification was run by the planner.
